title: queue_add.py silently drops a same-session, not-yet-pushed prior addition when called twice in a row (sync_queue_from_origin overwrites local-only items)
notes:
Discovered incidentally while filing two incidental issues (ISS-0641/GH-637 and ISS-0642/GH-638) during ISS-0101/GH-359's resolution. Ran `python3 tools/queue_add.py GH-637 ...` then `python3 tools/queue_add.py GH-638 ...` in immediate succession, without a `git push` between the two calls (both calls happened on a local feature branch mid-rebase, before the branch had been pushed). The SECOND call's `sync_queue_from_origin()` (tools/_queue_sync.py) fetched origin/main and returned origin's exact content as the base to mutate -- which does not yet contain GH-637 (added by the first call, never pushed) -- so GH-637 was silently dropped from the written-back file. Confirmed by direct inspection: after both calls, `grep -c 'GH-637' handoffs/global_queue.json` returned 0 while `GH-638` was present. Reproduced the same failure mode in reverse when attempting a workaround (adding GH-637 back, then re-running queue_add.py for GH-638, which then dropped GH-637 a second time) -- confirmed deterministic, not a one-off race.

Root cause: `sync_queue_from_origin()`'s docstring explicitly says it 'Falls back to local_fallback... if the fetch or remote read fails' but on a SUCCESSFUL fetch/read it unconditionally returns origin's content wholesale, with no merge step to preserve local-only items the caller's own in-memory copy already added within the same uncommitted session. This is by design for the cross-workspace race the tool documents (two independent checkouts each racing to add/update the SAME file) -- but it has an unintended side effect for the single-workspace, multiple-sequential-calls-before-push pattern, which is exactly how ISSUE-FIXER's Step 0.5 'incidental discovery' procedure is written (queue_add.py called once per incidental finding, potentially several times per run, before any push happens at Step Final).

Worked around for this run by writing both queue entries via a direct one-shot Python edit (read-modify-write, no sync-from-origin call) instead of two separate queue_add.py invocations. Not a data-loss risk for the CURRENT run since the drop was caught by manual verification before commit -- but the failure is silent (queue_add.py prints 'Added: GH-637' and exits 0 on the FIRST call, giving no indication it will later be discarded by a second call), so a less careful run would ship a Step 0.5 filing that silently never reaches the global queue, violating the No-Issue-Left-Local-Only directive without any error being surfaced anywhere.
candidate_resolution: Either (a) `sync_queue_from_origin()` gains a merge step: union origin's items with local_fallback's items by issue_id, preferring origin's copy of any KEY present in both (the existing conflict-safety property) but ADDING any issue_id present only in local_fallback (the missing case) -- this preserves both the cross-workspace safety guarantee and same-session sequential-call safety; or (b) `queue_add.py` pushes handoffs/global_queue.json to origin immediately after each successful write (matching the documented 'push the claim commit immediately' discipline already established for gh_claim.py per docs/anti-patterns.md's 2026-08-07 GH-542 entry), so the next call's fetch sees the previous call's addition. Option (a) is more robust since it doesn't require every caller to remember to commit+push between sequential queue_add.py calls, and it degrades gracefully if push access is unavailable mid-run.
resolution: Implemented candidate resolution (a): tools/_queue_sync.py's sync_queue_from_origin() now merges origin's items with local_fallback's items by issue_id via a new _merge_items_by_issue_id() helper, instead of returning origin's content wholesale. Origin's copy still wins for any issue_id present in both (preserves the original cross-workspace race protection this module exists for), but an issue_id present ONLY in local_fallback -- e.g. a same-session queue_add.py call for a different issue made moments earlier, not yet pushed -- is now carried over instead of silently dropped. Verified with two isolated Python-level reproductions: (1) the exact reported scenario (sequential same-session adds of two different issue_ids with no push between them) now preserves both; (2) the original conflict-safety guarantee still holds -- when the same issue_id exists in both origin and local with different state, origin's copy wins.
prevention: sync_queue_from_origin() is the single choke point all three queue tools (queue_add.py, queue_release.py, gh_claim.py) go through, so this fix covers all same-session multi-call sequences, not just queue_add.py's specific repro.

The merge is additive-only (never removes an item, never overwrites a shared-key item with the non-origin version), so it cannot reintroduce the original cross-workspace data-loss bug this module was built to fix.
